}}'''Alexander Lvovsky''' ({{langx|ru|Александр Исаевич Львовский}}; born 15 September, 1973, [[Moscow]], [[Russia]]) is an [[educator]] and [[experimental physicist]]. He currently holds a professorship at the [[University of Oxford]] and has contributed to [[quantum optics]] and its applications in technology. 

== Education and career ==

Lvovsky attended [[Moscow State School 57]], a school renowned for its focus on mathematics and physics. He earned his undergraduate degree in physics from the [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]] in 1993. He then attended [[Columbia University]] in New York City, completing a Master of Arts and Master of Philosophy in Physics in 1996 and a Ph.D. in 1998. His doctoral advisor was Sven R. Hartmann, and his dissertation focused on [[superradiance]] in atomic gases.<ref name=oxdept>{{cite web|title=Alexander Lvovsky. Professor.|url=https://www.physics.ox.ac.uk/our-people/lvovsky|website=Department of Physics, University of Oxford}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Research and teaching. Alexander Lvovsky. |url=https://users.physics.ox.ac.uk/~lvovsky/}}</ref>

After completing his Ph.D., Lvovsky was a postdoctoral researcher at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] (1998–1999). He subsequently joined the [[University of Konstanz]] in Germany as an [[Alexander_von_Humboldt_Foundation|Alexander von Humboldt postdoctoral fellow]] (1999–2001) and later headed an [[Emmy_Noether_Program|Emmy Noether]] research group in quantum-optical information technology until 2004.<ref>{{cite web |title=Experimente zur Erzeugung, Verarbeitung und Charakterisierung nichtklassischer Zustände des Lichtfelds |url=https://gepris.dfg.de/gepris/projekt/5348563 |website=Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG)}}</ref> In 2004, Lvovsky became a faculty member in the Department of Physics and Astronomy at the [[University of Calgary]], Canada, where he held a [[Canada Research Chair]]<ref>{{cite web |title=NSERC's Awards Database |url=https://www.nserc-crsng.gc.ca/ase-oro/Details-Detailles_eng.asp?id=385070 |website=Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada}}</ref> and advanced research in quantum information science. In 2018, he joined the University of Oxford as a Professor of Physics, continuing his work in quantum optics and optical computing.<ref name=oxdept/>

Lvovsky was involved in establishing the {{Interlanguage link|Russian Quantum Center|ru|3=Российский_квантовый_центр}} and led a research group there between 2013 and 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=People |url=https://rqc.ru/people |website=Russian Quantum Center |access-date=2025-04-10 |archive-date=2019-06-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190624081233/https://rqc.ru/people |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Research ==

Lvovsky's research focuses on quantum optics and its applications in technology and information processing, as well as optical computing and neural networks.<ref name=group>{{Cite web|url=https://quantech.group/|title=Quantum and optical technology. Research group home page}}</ref>

Examples of his contributions are
* Experiment on [[quantum_tomography|quantum homodyne tomography]] of the single-photon [[Fock state]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=A. I. Lvovsky, H. Hansen, T. Aichele, O. Benson, J. Mlynek and S. Schiller |title=Quantum State Reconstruction of the Single-Photon Fock State |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=2001 |volume=87 |issue=5 |article-number=050402|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.87.050402|pmid=11497753 |arxiv=quant-ph/0101051 |bibcode=2001PhRvL..87e0402L }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |title=Golfing with a Single Photon |journal=Physical Review Focus |date=1 August 2001 |volume=8 |page=7 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.87.050402 |url=http://focus.aps.org/story/v8/st7 |last1=Slayton |first1=Rebecca |last2=Hansen |first2=H. |last3=Aichele |first3=T. |last4=Benson |first4=O. |last5=Mlynek |first5=J. |last6=Schiller |first6=S. |issue=5 |pmid=11497753 |arxiv=quant-ph/0101051 }}</ref>
* Observation of [[quantum memory]] for [[squeezed light]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=J. Appel, E. Figueroa, D. Korystov, M. Lobino and A. I. Lvovsky |title=Quantum memory for squeezed light |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=2008 |volume=100 |issue=9 |article-number=093602 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.100.093602|pmid=18352710 |arxiv=0709.2258 |bibcode=2008PhRvL.100i3602A }}</ref>
* A method for optical [[quantum process tomography]] by [[coherent state]] probing.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=M. Lobino, D. Korystov, C. Kupchak, E. Figueroa, B. C. Sanders and A. I. == Teaching and outreach ==
Lvovsky's book ''Quantum Physics: An Introduction Based on Photons'' offers an alternative approach to teaching [[quantum mechanics]].  The book uses photon [[Photon polarization|polarization]] as the underlying physical system and teaches [[Quantum entanglement|entanglement]] early on in the course, rather than as an advanced concept. This is motivated by the understanding that entanglement is key to the inherent logic of quantum physics, particularly the nature of [[quantum measurement]], clarifying the role of [[Observer_(quantum_physics)|observer]] in it.<ref name=quantumbook>{{cite book |last1=Lvovsky |first1=A. I. |title=Quantum Physics: An Introduction Based on Photons |date=25 May 2018 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-662-56582-7}}</ref>  

Lvovsky established two educational outreach programmes providing small-group tutorials to senior [[secondary school]] students in the UK, delivered mainly by Oxford Physics [[undergraduate students]]:
* ''COMPOS'' (Comprehensive Oxford Mathematics and Physics Online School) focusses on developing the students' advanced problem-solving skills in mathematics and physics within the school syllabus.<ref>{{cite web|title=Comprehensive Oxford Mathematics and Physics Online School|url=https://compos.web.ox.ac.uk/|website=Department of Physics, University of Oxford}}</ref> 
* ''Quantum Club'' offers an academically rigorous quantum physics course, covering basic principles such as [[Hilbert space]] and measurement, as well as more advanced concepts including entanglement, [[quantum nonlocality|nonlocality]] and [[quantum teleportation|teleportation]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Oxford Quantum Club |url=https://www.physics.ox.ac.uk/engage/schools/secondary-schools/projects-and-mentoring/quantum-club|website=Department of Physics, University of Oxford}}</ref>

== Entrepreneurship ==

Lvovsky co-founded Lumai,<ref>{{cite web|title=LUMAI|url=https://lumai.ai/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |url=https://www.uktech.news/deep-tech/lumai-grant-20230215|journal=UKTN|title= Oxford optical computing startup Lumai awarded £1.1m grant|date=15 February 2023}}</ref> a spin-off company developing optical neural network technology aimed at high-speed, energy-efficient computing applications. 

== Awards ==

Lvovsky has received several awards, including the 2010 International Quantum Award.<ref>{{cite web|title=International Quantum Award|url=http://www.qcmc-conference.org/quantum-award.html}}</ref> He is a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?t=Division%20of%20Quantum%20Information%20Fellowship%0A&y=2025&af=true|title=APS Fellows Archive|website=American Physical Society}}</ref> and a Fellow of [[Optica (society)|Optica]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.optica.org/get_involved/awards_and_honors/fellow_members/elected_fellows/|title=Elected Fellows|website=Optica}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Lvovsky is married to Bhavya Rawal and they are raising three children.<ref name=quantumbook/>
